drivingQuestion: Why is the owner believed about blemishes in animal tithe?
outcomeNote: The owner is believed since he could have blemished his entire flock beforehand.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא! מִי יָדַע הֵי נָפֵיק?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «What is the reason» that even the owner is deemed credible to testify? The reason is «that had he wanted, he could have caused a blemish in it initially,» in a permitted manner, before tithing his animals. The Gemara raises a difficulty: But when he leads his animals out of the gate in order to tithe them, «does he know which» of them «will emerge» as the tenth, that you say he could have initially blemished that specific animal before it assumed the tithe status?

segments.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ בְּרֵישׁ עַשְׂרָה, ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא! אֶלָּא דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא (בכולי) [בְּכוּלֵּיהּ] עֶדְרֵיהּ.
segments.en: «And if you would say» that «he» intentionally «leads» an animal «out as the head of the ten,» i.e., so that it is the last of ten to emerge, one may not do so, as «the Merciful One states: “He shall not search whether it be good or bad”» (Leviticus 27:33), which teaches that the animal tithe may not be led out intentionally but must exit of its own accord. «Rather,» this is the meaning of the Gemara’s initial answer: The reason is «that had he wanted, he could have caused a blemish in his entire flock,» in a permitted manner, before leading them through the gate in order to tithe them.
